title: Artisan vs. Gong Engage: Which fits your team?
summary: Gong Engage is a sales-engagement module humans run inside Gong's platform. Artisan's Ava runs outbound end to end. Here's how to choose in 2026.
body_markdown:
Both touch outbound, but they play different roles. Gong Engage is a sales-engagement module inside Gong's Revenue AI platform, where reps run sequences informed by Gong's call analysis. Artisan's Ava is an autonomous AI business development representative (BDR) who runs the whole outbound motion herself. One augments your reps, and the other owns the job.


## Artisan vs. Gong Engage at a glance


These are not the same category of product. This table maps your situation to the better fit.

## What does Gong Engage do well?


Gong earned its reputation, and Engage inherits it. The core Gong platform is the category standard for conversation intelligence. It records, transcribes, and analyzes sales calls, then identifies what is working across deals and reps. Engage, launched in 2023, is the sales-engagement layer that puts this intelligence to work, so a rep's sequences and outreach can reflect what Gong learned from actual conversations. This conversation-intelligence-to-engagement loop is Engage's real differentiator, and no pure sequencer matches it, because they do not own the call data underneath. For the wider category, see[the best sales engagement platforms](https://www.artisan.co/blog/the-best-sales-engagement-platforms) and[the best Gong Engage alternatives](https://www.artisan.co/blog/the-best-gong-engage-alternatives) .


The scale backs it up. Gong's ARR passed $500M as of May 2026, growing more than 55% year over year, with over 5,000 customers. Enterprises trust it, and for a team whose motion revolves around call intelligence and coaching, having engagement built on the same platform is a clean architecture. If Gong is already your system of record for calls, Engage is a natural extension.


Two honest limits. First, Engage is a module rather than a standalone product. It is sold as part of the Gong platform, so adopting it means buying into a mandatory platform fee (reported around $5K to $50K a year depending on size) plus per-seat costs (reported around $1,200 to $3,000/user/year), all gated behind a sales process, with the Engage-only price not disclosed. Second, at sequencing depth it is newer and less mature than a dedicated engagement veteran like Outreach. For comparisons there, see[Artisan vs. Outreach](https://www.artisan.co/blog/artisan-vs-outreach) ,[Apollo vs. Outreach](https://www.artisan.co/blog/apollo-vs-outreach-which-should-you-choose) , and[the best Outreach alternatives](https://www.artisan.co/blog/the-best-outreach-alternatives) . Structurally, Engage is a tool your reps run. It makes them better, and it does not do the job for them.


## How is Artisan's Ava different?


Ava is not a better toolset for reps. She is an autonomous AI BDR who owns the outbound job end to end. She finds best-fit leads across a database of over 250 million B2B professionals in over 200 countries using natural-language search, ideal customer profile (ICP) filters, and intent signals; enriches and ranks them by likelihood of converting with waterfall email and phone data that charges only on success; launches personalized multichannel campaigns across email, social media, and dialer call steps; tests dozens of message variations and shifts volume toward what converts; handles every reply by qualifying, answering objections from a knowledge base, and chasing follow-ups; and books meetings on reps' calendars with CRM-owner routing.


This is the categorical difference. Gong Engage gives a human rep a smart place to run sequences. Ava runs the sequences, and the sourcing, and the dialing, and the replies. You set your ICP and the guardrails, and she executes the motion. Personalization runs from light to agentic, with research-agent swarms for hard criteria, at a scale a rep team cannot match by hand. Two people in the same Artisan campaign receive two completely different messages, where a legacy sequencer changes only the name and title. For this category, see[email sequencing software](https://www.artisan.co/blog/email-sequencing-software) .


## Which one sources net-new pipeline?


This is a real gap, and it favors Artisan. Gong Engage works the contacts and accounts already in your world. It is an engagement layer, and the intelligence it runs on comes from calls you are already having. It does not source net-new leads at scale from a first-party database. This is not its job.


Ava's job starts earlier. She sources net-new best-fit leads from a database of over 250 million B2B professionals, plus Artisan Local Data covering over 250 million local businesses, then enriches and works them. So these two products sit at different points in the funnel. Gong Engage sharpens outreach to people already in motion, while Ava fills the top of the funnel and runs it all the way to a booked meeting. For a team that needs pipeline created instead of only engaged, this difference is decisive.


## What about call intelligence, is that not Gong's strength?


It is, at the platform level, and Artisan does not pretend to be a full conversation-intelligence suite across every rep's calls. Gong's depth of call analysis and coaching across a whole team is best in class.


That said, Artisan is not blind on calls. Ava's dialer runs calls as steps inside multichannel sequences, with live AI talking points loaded before the call connects, live transcription, auto-classified outcomes, and an AI-drafted follow-up email after each answered call. So on the outbound Ava runs, she has her own call intelligence built in. The distinction is scope. Gong analyzes conversations across your entire revenue org, including account executive and customer calls, while Artisan applies call intelligence to the outbound motion it operates. If org-wide conversation intelligence and coaching is your central need, that is Gong's to own. If you want AI to dial the outbound calls for your reps, that is Ava.


## How do the economics compare?


Gong Engage's cost is a package. You are buying into the Gong platform, which means a mandatory platform fee (reported roughly $5K to $50K a year by company size) plus per-seat licenses (reported roughly $1,200 to $3,000/user/year), all gated and bundled, with the Engage-only line item not disclosed. For a large team already committed to Gong, this is absorbed into an existing contract. For a team buying engagement alone, it is a heavy entry point, and every added rep adds seat cost. For the full cost picture, see[Gong Engage pricing and reviews](https://www.artisan.co/blog/gong-engage-pricing-and-reviews) .


Artisan is usage-based. You pay for the work Ava performs rather than for seats, and you can trial her for free. Because Ava does the work, output does not scale with headcount the way a per-seat engagement tool does. Chain of Events, the team behind RAISE Summit, replaced the workload of five human BDRs with Ava on a $28K annual investment, and sourced over $700K in ARR in six months, a 20x return.


## Choose Gong Engage if...


-


You already run Gong and want your engagement tied directly to your conversation intelligence and coaching.


-


Call intelligence across your entire revenue team is your primary need, and engagement is a valued extension of it.


-


You are standardizing a large rep organization on one revenue platform and prefer everything in the same system.


-


Your reps will run the sequences, and you want them to run on the smartest call data available.


Gong is a proven, large-scale platform with best-in-class conversation intelligence. If it is already your center of gravity, Engage is a coherent addition.


## Choose Artisan if...


-


You want AI to run the outbound motion end to end instead of a better toolset for your reps to operate.


-


You need to source net-new pipeline at scale, not only engage contacts already in your world.


-


You would rather pay for the work performed than buy into a mandatory platform fee and per-seat licenses.


-


You want autonomy controls, escalation rules, and an audit trail over an AI that owns sourcing through booking.


## What customers say


SaaStr frames the shift from tool to worker directly. Amelia Lerutte, Chief AI Officer at SaaStr, says: "Email has always been our number one driver. Artisan is now neck-and-neck in both output and closed-won revenue." In roughly six weeks, Ava sent 6,892 emails, 3,574 of them to new leads, at a 3.6% positive response rate. CookUnity's Bruno Didier adds that "Ava runs highly targeted outreach at a scale we could never reach with a human-only team." This is the line between a product that helps reps engage and one that does the engaging.


## Frequently asked questions


### Is Gong Engage better than Artisan?


For conversation-intelligence-driven engagement inside an existing Gong deployment, Engage is a strong, natural fit, and its intelligence-to-outreach loop is a real edge. Engage is a tool reps run, though, and it does not source net-new leads. Artisan's Ava owns the whole outbound motion autonomously, from sourcing to booking, so the better choice depends on whether you want a smarter toolset or an AI employee.


### Can I buy Gong Engage on its own?


Not really. Engage is a module inside Gong's Revenue AI platform, sold as part of the platform with a mandatory platform fee plus per-seat costs, all gated. The Engage-only price is not disclosed. Artisan's outbound platform is standalone and usage-based, so you pay for the work Ava performs, and you can trial her for free.


### How much does Gong Engage cost?


Gong's pricing is gated. Third-party reports put the mandatory platform fee at roughly $5K to $50K a year by company size, plus per-seat licenses around $1,200 to $3,000/user/year, bundled together. The Engage-specific line item is not published, so you would receive a quote through Gong's sales process.


### Does Artisan do conversation intelligence?


Artisan does call intelligence on the outbound Ava runs: live AI talking points before the call connects, live transcription, auto-classified outcomes, and an AI-drafted follow-up email. It is not a full org-wide conversation-intelligence suite across every account executive and customer call the way Gong is. If org-wide conversation intelligence and coaching is your central need, Gong owns that. If you want AI to dial the outbound calls for your reps, that is Ava.


### Which one sources new leads?


Artisan. Ava sources net-new best-fit leads from a database of over 250 million B2B professionals, then enriches, sequences, dials, and books. Gong Engage works contacts and accounts already in your system and does not source net-new leads at scale. It is an engagement layer rather than a data-and-sourcing engine.


### Which is more autonomous?


Artisan, by design. Gong Engage is operated by human reps. Ava runs the motion herself, with autonomy set as a dial: review-and-approve every message, objections-only replies, or full autonomy, plus plain-language escalation rules and a full audit trail. Over 90% of Artisan customers run Ava autonomously.


## The bottom line


If Gong is already your platform and you want engagement wired to your conversation intelligence, Gong Engage is a sensible extension, and its call-data edge is real. If you want an AI that sources, sequences, dials, and books on its own instead of a smarter toolset your reps still operate, that is Artisan.
